kernels.name: qualifying_child_residence_gate
kernels.query_clause: Whether the individual is the taxpayer's qualifying child under §152(c)(1), limited to the mandatory same-principal-place-of-abode condition in §152(c)(1)(B).
kernels.source_quote: (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year,

value.rationale: The agricultural kernel evaluates only §3306(a)(2)(A), not the alternative day-and-worker test. It counts distinct events whose payer is the queried claimant and whose supplied facts expressly identify the full amount as wages for “agricultural labor”; it does not independently classify remuneration as wages. A known $20,000 witness establishes Entailment even if other relevant events remain unresolved. Contradiction requires an explicitly exhaustive event set and no unresolved relevant allocation. Literal descriptions other than the supplied positive or negative agricultural-labor phrases remain unresolved. The residence kernel treats the query year as the taxable-year period directed by the task, clips inclusive residence intervals to that year, and applies the strict “more than one-half” test. It produces only a necessary-gate Contradiction, and only from an explicitly complete, unambiguous principal-abode history. Passing the residence condition does not establish relationship, age, joint-return, or any other §152(c)(1) requirement. The supplied source contains no exception to the residence condition, so none is added.
